messages:
alex: Ran the multi-GPU inference sweep across eu-west and us-west pools. PCIe nodes show a much worse 99p tail under concurrent load vs SXM. nvlink nodes look stable. Posting quick notes.

maria: Can you drop the perf numbers (batch, seq len, quant) and the test harness?

alex: batch sizes 1/2/4/8, seq 512, model=sm7b-qa-8bit (8-bit quant). Throughput similar across cards but 99p latency diverges under >60 concurrent requests: PCIe 99p ~250ms, SXM 99p ~90ms. p50/p95 pretty close. Chart here: http://short.url/bench123 (csv and graphs).

damon: Did you try pinning processes to a CPU socket? My money is on a NUMA hop when CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES mapping crosses host CPU domains.

alex: Yup — numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 reduced PCIe 99p by ~30%. Also toggled `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` ordering, no effect unless we bind CPUs.

maria: Any NCCL or PCIe P2P notes?

alex: On problematic nodes `nvidia-smi topo -m` shows some GPU pairs are PX (via PCIe switch) instead of P2P/NVLink. That introduces extra memcpy hops. SXM machines are full NVLink mesh so no hop.

karen: So path difference is expected, but 250ms is high. Could be host-side stalls. Did you check interrupts/CPU contention on pinned cores?

alex: Spikes align with CPU steal/softirq on the same cores handling the GPU driver. When we isolate IRQs and move user threads off those cores, tail improves.

yousef: For KV cache sharing, can we avoid cross-socket sharing? Replicate KV across GPUs or shard so each GPU keeps local state to reduce cross-socket sync.

maria: And what about quantization? 8-bit introduced some extra host<->device syncs during dequantization maybe? Any quality regressions observed?

alex: Quant adds a small compute overhead but not the dominant factor for the tail. We ran a quality eval on 4 vs 8 bit — minor score differences, no obvious regressions for this model family. Will attach eval csv.

bench-bot: Trace uploaded -> s3://redwood-bench/1755554322/trace.tar.gz (perf traces, nvtop logs, `nvidia-smi topo -m` outputs).

damon: Next experiments to try: 1) repro with IRQ isolation 2) enable CUDA MPS on PCIe nodes 3) test kernel 6.1 vs 5.15 (we had memcpy regressions on older stable kernels) 4) force no-uvm in kernel for one run to check UVM overhead

alex: Plan set. I'll run overnight across both regions, include per-token latency and p50/p95/p99/p99.9, and a csv of per-request stack samples. Also will try replicating KV cache to avoid cross-socket fetches.

maria: :thumbsup: Please include machine SKUs and nv driver versions. If region-specific, we should consider routing critical customers to SXM pools until we have mitigations.

karen: Agreed, temporary routing rule sounds reasonable. Keep an eye on cost impact if we shift traffic.

alex: Will update with full numbers tomorrow. Short-term note: numactl binding + IRQ isolation produced the largest immediate improvement on PCIe nodes.
